sections.h2: Where is Melrose, Massachusetts, and what kind of city is it?
sections.html:
Melrose is a small city in Middlesex County, about seven miles north of Boston. Wikipedia describes it as sitting in the middle of the triangle formed by Interstate 93, Interstate 95 and U.S. Route 1, and it borders Malden, Saugus, Stoneham and Wakefield.

The city covers only 4.77 square miles, so almost every house sits close to a pond, a park or a train stop. The 2020 census counted 29,817 residents and 12,614 housing units, with 3.7% of those units vacant. Melrose peaked at 33,180 people in 1970, slipped for four decades, then grew 10.5% between 2010 and 2020.

For a seller, that history shows up in the housing stock. The first lots were carved out of farmland in the second half of the 1800s, so plenty of Melrose houses are old, and old houses bring their own checklists at sale time.

sections.h2: How did Melrose get its name and its shape?
sections.html:
Melrose began as North Malden, a lightly settled farming area that became its own town in 1850 and took its name from Melrose, Scotland. The Boston and Maine Railroad had added three stops by 1845, and Boston workers who wanted a country setting started commuting from here.

  • 1850: North Malden splits from Malden and becomes the Town of Melrose.
  • 1853: The town annexes the highlands from Stoneham, which set today's borders.
  • 1873: The town hall is built.
  • 1899 to 1900: Melrose becomes the 33rd city in Massachusetts, and Levi S. Gould takes office as first mayor on January 1, 1900.
  • 1982: Downtown Melrose is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

Those three railroad stops are still the commuter rail stations on the Haverhill Line and all three remain in service today.

sections.h2: Which Melrose neighborhoods come up most often?
sections.html:
Wikipedia lists eight named neighborhoods in Melrose, and buyers and sellers tend to place a house by one of them.

  • Cedar Park and Wyoming, which share names with commuter rail stops
  • Melrose Highlands, the part annexed from Stoneham
  • Downtown Melrose, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1982
  • Horace Mann, East Side and Mount Hood on the eastern side of the city
  • Oak Grove and Pine Banks, near the Malden line and Pine Banks Park

Ell Pond sits near the center of the city. Swains Pond and Towners Pond are on the east side near Mount Hood Golf Club, and the eastern reaches of the Middlesex Fells Reservation also fall inside the city line. A house near water or park land can show different grading, drainage and basement conditions than one on a hilltop, so a seller should expect a buyer's inspector to look closely at the lower floors.

sections.h2: How do people get around Melrose and into Boston?
sections.html:
Melrose has no major highway of its own, only a short stretch of Route 99, and relies on nearby roads and the MBTA instead. Residents reach Route 1 in Saugus, Interstate 93 in Stoneham, Route 16 in Everett and Route 128 or Interstate 95 in Wakefield.

Three Haverhill Line commuter rail stations serve the city: Melrose Highlands, Melrose/Cedar Park and Wyoming Hill. MBTA bus routes 131, 132 and 137 also run through, and the Orange Line terminal at Oak Grove sits just across the line in Malden. Access to Boston by rail is part of why Melrose has long been a commuter suburb.

MelroseWakefield Hospital, a 234-bed non-profit, is the best-known institution in the city, and Wikipedia notes it was home to the world's first cochlear implant. The Milano Senior Center runs programs for older residents.

The Melrose school district operates the Franklin Early Childhood Center, five elementary schools (Roosevelt, Lincoln, Winthrop, Hoover and Horace Mann), Melrose Veterans Memorial Middle School and Melrose High School. St. Mary of the Annunciation runs a private elementary school. The city has also appeared on screen, with scenes from The Town, Spirited and Beetlejuice Beetlejuice filmed locally.

sections.h2: When are Melrose property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Melrose bills real estate tax quarterly on a fiscal year that runs July 1 to June 30. The treasurer's page lists the FY2027 schedule below, and the first two bills are estimates while the last two are based on assessed values.

QuarterDue date
1st quarterAugust 3, 2026
2nd quarterNovember 2, 2026
3rd quarterFebruary 1, 2027
4th quarterMay 3, 2027

The assessor values property as of January 1 each year. The office is on the first floor of City Hall at 562 Main Street and can be reached at 781-979-4104. It also notes that field inspections are underway across the city as part of its work keeping assessments current. See the Melrose assessor page and the real estate tax page for current details.

sections.h2: What steps come before closing on a Melrose house?
sections.html:
A Melrose seller needs a fire department smoke and carbon monoxide certificate, a title search, and usually a real estate attorney. These steps come from Massachusetts state sources, and Melrose officials handle the local parts.

  • Smoke and CO certificate: The Department of Fire Services says you need a certificate of compliance from the local fire department when you sell or transfer a home. Call as soon as you have a closing date, because the requirements depend on when the house was built and when the last building permit was issued.
  • Alarm age: Battery-powered smoke alarms over 10 years old, or with no manufacture date, must be replaced with sealed 10-year photoelectric units that have a hush feature.
  • Municipal lien certificate: Melrose offers an online request for these certificates through the treasurer and collector.
  • Attorney and title: The Trial Court Law Libraries say real estate attorneys are a regular part of buying and selling in Massachusetts, by law and practice.
  • Deed tax: Massachusetts charges a deeds excise under Chapter 64D, Section 1, set per $500 of sale price. Ask the registry or your attorney for the current figure.

The state also bars sellers from conditioning an offer on a buyer's waiver of a home inspection for certain residential sales, under 760 CMR 74. Your attorney can tell you whether your sale falls under that rule.

sections.h2: What do Melrose sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Melrose sellers most often face the age of the house, which drives repair lists, alarm upgrades and inspection findings. Older homes can need electrical, roof or foundation work that a buyer financing with a mortgage may ask to have fixed before closing.

Others are selling an inherited house, handling an estate, or managing a rental with tenants still in place. Each of those adds paperwork, and the timeline can stretch while the fire certificate, lien certificate and title work come together. Cash Home Buyers works with owners in these situations and can look at a Melrose property as it stands.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Melrose?
sections.html:
A cash sale removes the mortgage approval step, which is where many conventional deals slow down. You tell us about the house, we review it, and if you choose to move forward the same Massachusetts requirements still apply.

  • You still need the fire department certificate of compliance.
  • The deed is still recorded at the registry of deeds.
  • Taxes owed to the city show up on the municipal lien certificate and are settled at closing.
  • A closing attorney still handles the title work.

faqs.q: Is Melrose a town or a city?
faqs.a: Melrose is a city. It became the Town of Melrose in 1850 and was incorporated as a city at the turn of 1900, with a mayor and an eleven-member city council.

faqs.q: What is the Melrose residential tax rate?
faqs.a: The FY2026 residential rate is $11.47 per $1,000 of assessed value, and the commercial, industrial and personal property rate is $20.61, according to the City of Melrose assessor page.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell a house in Melrose?
faqs.a: Yes. The Massachusetts Department of Fire Services says a seller needs a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing the alarms meet requirements for a sale or transfer. The department charges a fee, so call the Melrose fire department to schedule.

faqs.q: Which commuter rail stations serve Melrose?
faqs.a: Three Haverhill Line stations serve Melrose: Melrose Highlands, Melrose/Cedar Park and Wyoming Hill. The Orange Line stop at Oak Grove is in neighboring Malden.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Melrose house with tenants or repairs needed?
faqs.a: Yes, you can sell a Melrose house as it is, with repairs undone or tenants in place. The smoke and CO certificate, title work and tax settlement still have to be handled, so ask your attorney about the order of steps.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Melrose assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Melrose Assessment Department at 781-979-4104. It is on the first floor of City Hall at 562 Main Street, open Monday through Thursday 8:30 am to 4 pm and Friday 8:30 am to 12:30 pm.
